summary: For every number in the range, raise each digit to the number of digits and compare the sum with the number itself (T2 — digit manipulation). Turning the number into a string gives both the digits and their count.

blocks.title: Read L and R from one line
blocks.text: Both numbers are on ONE line, so `split()` + `map(int, …)`.

blocks.title: Collect the matches
blocks.text: We gather them in a list so we can print them on one line — or print `None` if there are none.

blocks.title: Digits and the power
blocks.text: `range(L, R + 1)` includes R. `str(x)` gives the digits; `len` gives how many there are, which is the power.

blocks.title: Is it an Armstrong number?
blocks.text: Sum every digit raised to the power and compare with x. Every 1-digit number passes (5¹ = 5).

blocks.title: Print the list or None
blocks.text: `print("Armstrong numbers:", *found)` prints the numbers separated by spaces. An empty list must print `Armstrong numbers: None` instead of an empty line.

complexity: Time O((R − L) × digits) with R ≤ 10⁵ → about 500,000 digit operations.
pitfalls: Using a fixed power of 3 instead of the digit count.
Printing nothing when there are no matches.
